description: What one index run did, in the same numbers `fathom index --stats` prints as a table. Owner: `e1.4`, surfaced by `e1.10`.

graph.description: The module graph pass (`e3.11`, `reco-dlp`): what one revision's graph cost and what the pass refused. `null` when the run did not ask for a graph — `--no-graph`, or `graph.enabled = false` — because "not asked" is not the same statement as "asked, and the store already held every revision".

anchors.description: Revisions written as full anchors: the first of a pass, a break in the first-parent chain, or a chain that reached `graph.chain_full_every`. An anchor costs one manifest row plus the chunks that are new.

edges.description: Edges in the newest revision this pass wrote, as the graph stores them: module-to-module, import, wildcard and package-granular kinds together.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall time of the graph pass alone. It is also its own entry in `phases_ms`, and this is the number a slow index is argued about.

modules.description: Modules in the newest revision this pass wrote, after `graph.ignored_dirs` is applied.

nodes.description: Nodes in the newest revision: modules and their exported symbols.

notices.description: What the pass refused and why: a knob that did not parse, a file over `extract.max_file_bytes`, a blob git would not serve. Capped at six, because the count is `unavailable` and the notices are examples.

outside_window.description: Owed revisions older than `graph.window`, which the lane therefore holds no graph for (`reco-r3x`). Not a queue: at this configuration no later pass writes them either, and the only way to graph them is to raise the window (or set it to `0`, which is every owed revision). Printed as data rather than on every run because it is what the configuration chose, not work left undone.

partial.description: Why the pass stopped short of graphing everything — revisions older than `graph.window`, the corpus cap, a cancellation — or null when there was nothing to stop short of. A graph that stopped halfway must not read as a graph that is finished; a run that wrote nothing because the window already covers everything says nothing at all.

revisions.description: Revisions this pass wrote a graph for.

reset_rows.description: Derived graph rows deleted because `--refresh` asked the lane to be re-derived (ADR-004 §9.5: derived data is recomputed, not migrated). Zero on every other run.

skipped.description: Files the tree held that are not modules: not one of the six grammars, or under `graph.ignored_dirs`.

unavailable.description: Modules kept in the graph with no structural record: over `extract.max_file_bytes`, not UTF-8, or an object git would not serve. Counted, never guessed at.

intent.description: What the intent capture (`e4.2`) recorded for this run, and what stream it came from. Every bucket is printed, including the empty one and the 'nothing recorded' one: missing intent is a state, and a state that only appears when it is non-empty is a state a reviewer never learns to read.

recorded.description: Episodes whose intent arrived as text - a prompt, an intent line, a task, a plan item.

from_hook.description: Of those, how many came from the harness stream rather than from a commit trailer.

digest_only.description: Episodes whose only intent evidence is a prompt digest: a request happened, its text was not sent.

none.description: Episodes with nothing recorded anywhere - the ticket's normal state, counted rather than hidden.

harness.description: The event stream the capture read. `events_file` is printed even when it does not exist, so 'no intent' can be told apart from 'no hooks' without a second command.

events_file.description: Where the stream was looked for, redacted to a repository-relative path.

exists.description: Whether a stream file was there at all.

turns.description: Turns the ledger holds, trimmed ones excluded.

events.description: Events the reader accepted on this pass.

refused.description: Lines the reader refused. Kept beside `turns` because an empty file and an unreadable file produce the same zero, and only one of them is normal.

notices.description: One line per thing the reader found and could not use, including a stream that exists but would not parse: 'no stream' and 'unreadable stream' are different reasons for the same empty intent tally, and only one of them is the repository's fault.

unreadable.description: Every commit this store cannot read out of the object database, named by id and by what the read said. A damaged or filter-cloned repository; the remedy is `git fsck`, never a fathom repair.

commit.description: The commit fathom tried to index.

seen_utc.description: When the index last tried this commit.

nothing_new.description: True when the run compared the refs with the store's last snapshot, found they said the same thing, and skipped the history walk, the analysis pass and the episode rebuild instead of repeating them (`reco-7tc`). Read `commits.walked: 0` with this in mind: 0 with true here is a warm store with nothing to do, and 0 with false is a repository with no history.

phases_ms.description: Where the run's wall clock went, in whole milliseconds, in run order (`reco-66q`). The keys are the phases of `fathom_analyze::index::run`, so a report that says "45 s" also says which 45 seconds they were.

store.description: Repository-relative path to the store this run wrote.

prune.description: What `--prune` removed (or, on `--dry-run`, would have): the commit rows no ref reaches, what cascaded with them, and what the review guard refused to touch. `null` when `--prune` was not passed — 'nothing was asked' is not the same statement as 'nothing was dead'.

commits_removed.description: `git_commit` rows removed: every one of them provably unreachable.

dry_run.description: True when `--dry-run` was passed. Every number below is then what a real prune *would* do, computed by the same statements rather than a second estimate.

episodes_removed.description: Episode rows that lost their last member to the prune and carried no decision, review or relink, so nothing pointed at them.

files_removed.description: `git_commit_file` rows that went with those commits.

refusal.description: Why the store deleted nothing because it could not tell dead rows from live ones — a break in the stored parent chain, or no ref tip to walk from. A refusal is a stated partial, not an error: the verb still exits 0.

sample.description: Up to twelve of the commit ids involved, newest first.

withheld_reviewed.description: Dead commits left in place because a review state or a mirrored ledger entry points at them (ADR-004 §8.2). Counted, never silently subtracted.

withheld_undecidable.description: Pairs with `refusal`: the rows that would have been candidates had the store been able to judge.

complexity_fill.description: The index-time complexity pass (ADR-007 §9.7, `e8.4`): what it counted, what it refused and why, how much file content it read, and which ceiling stopped it if one did. Not an analyzer in `analyzers`, because its memo is the column it writes rather than a cache lookup — `rows` is not a lookup count and there is no hit rate to report. A consumer that needs to know whether this index measured complexity has to be able to tell 'nothing owed a figure' from 'the budget ran out', and this is the only place the two differ.

rows.description: File rows the pass answered, including the ones it declined.

measured.description: Rows that ended with at least one figure.

items.description: One §7.1 reason code and how many sides of a file row refused on it.

code.description: The reason code, as ADR-007 §7.1 spells it.

rows.description: Sides of a file row that printed `?` for this code.

refused.description: Refusals by reason code, sorted by code. The durable count of the same names lives in the `counter` table as `complexity.refused.<code>`; this is the run's own share of it.

bytes_read.description: Bytes of blob content inflated for a figure — the quantity `extract.complexity.max_run_bytes` bounds.

base_reused.description: Base-side figures taken from the first parent's stored row instead of from a read, which is what makes ADR-007 §9.2's telescoping identity a property of the code.

run_reused.description: Sides answered from a figure this same run already counted for the path, instead of inflating the blob and parsing it again. The blob id has to equal the one the figure was counted from, so a miss costs a read and nothing else; on a cold index this is the only memo there is, because nothing is stored to borrow yet.

ms.description: Milliseconds this pass's own work took, summed over the commits it filled. The same accumulated quantity `extract.complexity.max_run_ms` bounded, so the reported number is the bounded number.

written.description: File rows whose complexity columns were written.

missing.description: Writes that named no file row — a fill racing `fathom index --prune`. Counted, not fatal.

declined.description: The config key of the ceiling that stopped the pass, or null when nothing did. Its rows print `?` with `scan_budget` and stay owed, so raising the key and re-indexing fills them.

ceilings.description: The three ceilings the pass was obeying, spent or not — the numbers a reader needs in order to judge the ones beside them. Printed as text beside the run report's line, for the same reason.

max_file_bytes.description: `extract.complexity.max_file_bytes` in force: the largest blob counted for one row.

max_run_bytes.description: `extract.complexity.max_run_bytes` in force: the run's byte budget. `0` declines the whole pass.

max_run_ms.description: `extract.complexity.max_run_ms` in force: the pass's own clock, in milliseconds. `0` declines the whole pass.

title: fathom index --json

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: OK
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb answered, and the index describes HEAD

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: ERROR
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a rev that names nothing, an unimplemented verb, a rejected argument value

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: USAGE
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: clap rejected the command line (bad flag, unknown verb, missing value)

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: NOT_A_REPOSITORY
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: --root is not a git repository, or `.git` is unreadable

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: CONFIG_INVALID
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: `fathom.toml` failed the schema, or a value is the wrong type

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: CANCELLED
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a cancel handle was pulled mid-run

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: FEATURE_ABSENT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb needs a feature this binary was not built with
